title: External Rotation at 90° Abduction

checks.basis: AAOS normal external rotation 0-90 deg; 60+ allows for the ~10 deg uncertainty of estimating rotation from a front camera
checks.label: Rotation from neutral

checks.basis: upper arm at shoulder height (90 +- 20 deg of abduction), the 90/90 test position
checks.label: Shoulder elevation

checks.basis: elbow held near a right angle (90 +- 30 deg) for 90/90 rotation
checks.label: Elbow angle

checks.basis: trunk side lean under 10 deg (trunk lean is the usual compensation for limited shoulder range)
checks.label: Lateral trunk lean

cues.ERR_ELBOW_ANGLE: Keep your elbow bent at a right angle.
cues.ERR_ELBOW_DROP: Keep your elbow up at shoulder height.
cues.ERR_ELBOW_HIGH: Keep your elbow level with your shoulder, not above it.
cues.ERR_LOW_ROTATION: Rotate your forearm further, as far as is comfortable.
cues.ERR_TRUNK_LEAN: Keep your trunk upright; don't lean to the side.

source: Clinical thresholds (AAOS / Norkin & White norms, common compensation limits); false alarms measured on MobiPhysio videos physiotherapists scored >= 90 (Iqbal et al., Harvard Dataverse 2025, CC0)
